messages.content: Help me execute a performance test in Java with 500 iterations, outputting the results to a `System.out` stream, and using command-line arguments that specify a wait time of 2 minutes?

function.name: thrcputime002_runIt
function.description: Executes a performance test by running a specific thread for a given number of iterations and logs the output to the provided PrintStream. It also handles synchronization and status checks before, during, and after the thread execution. Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax.

argv.description: An array of command-line arguments to configure the test, including wait time and number of iterations. In the format of -waitTime, <waitTime>, -iterations, <iterations> This is Java Array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation.

out.description: The PrintStream to which the test output will be written. This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation.

We have a tool function thrcputime002_runIt that takes argv as string (Java array type parameter in string representation) and out as string (any Java object in string representation). We need to call this function with appropriate arguments.

We need to provide argv: "-waitTime, 120000, -iterations, 500" maybe? Wait time in milliseconds? They said wait time of 2 minutes. So 2 minutes = 120 seconds = 120000 ms. But the function expects an array of command-line arguments to configure the test, including wait time and number of iterations. Format: -waitTime, <waitTime>, -iterations, <iterations>. So we need to pass a string representation of a Java array type. For example: "new String[]{\"-waitTime\", \"120000\", \"-iterations\", \"500\"}". That is the string representation of a Java array type. The out parameter should be "System.out". So we call the function with those parameters.

Thus we produce a JSON object with keys argv and out. The argv value is a string representation of a Java array type. So we do:

{
  "argv": "new String[]{\"-waitTime\", \"120000\", \"-iterations\", \"500\"}",
  "out": "System.out"
}

We then call the function.
